Definition: , and genitive case, ὕδατος, etc. from the base of G5205; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively:--water.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hýdōr is the word for water. In Matthew 3:11, the text says "I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance." In Mark 1:8, the text says "I indeed have baptized you with water."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hýdōr tells me that creation is God's handiwork, and it still speaks of Him to anyone willing to look. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
